english.title: Fail to preserve register / produce register to inspector and allow him to take copies
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),

(A)_[being a person keeping a register pursuant to regulations under Section 69(6) of the Agriculture Act 1970, failed to preserve the register for the prescribed period, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PRESCRIBED PERIOD..)]_
(B)_[being a person who had a register pursuant to regulations under Section 69(6) of the Agriculture Act 1970 in your possession or under your control failed on demand by an inspector to produce it for inspection and allow copies of it to be taken]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 69(7) of the Agriculture Act 1970.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
fail to produce a register to inspector and allow him to take copies

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.standardstatementoffacts:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant,

(A)_[being a person keeping a register pursuant to regulations under Section 69(6) of the Agriculture Act 1970, failed to preserve the register for the prescribed period.]_
(B)_[being a person who had a register pursuant to regulations under Section 69(6) of the Agriculture Act 1970 in his possession or under his control failed on demand by an inspector to produce it for inspection and allow copies of it to be taken.]_
(C)_[being a person who had a register pursuant to regulations under Section 69(6) of the Agriculture Act 1970 in her possession or under her control failed on demand by an inspector to produce it for inspection and allow copies of it to be taken.]_

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale .

Time Limit on Prosecutions
Six months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
